recipes.projection: Blended projection = weighted mean of Sleeper app x1, FantasyPros x1, CBS Sports x1, ESPN fantasy x1, DraftKings points converted from each source's own stat lines. Weights renormalise over the sources that cover each player; coverage is the covering weight as a share of the total enabled weight. Coverage under 50% keeps the number from the sources that do cover the player and is flagged "thin"; it is never pulled toward a typical score for the salary. No coverage leaves the projection blank, flagged "no projection", unless the injury report lists the player as out, on IR, doubtful or suspended, in which case the projection is 0.
recipes.ownership: Own% is the average, by source weight, of the numbers Weekly findings file, Footballguys percent rostered and RotoWire projected roster % published for the DraftKings main slate; numbers for any other site or slate are never used. Stokastic DK cheat sheet is downloaded, stored and shown in its own column, but never averaged into Own% (weight 0). A number Adam types into the Own% cell replaces the published one for that player. A player with no published number is left blank: the app never estimates ownership, so game popularity exists only where a real number does.
recipes.scoring: DraftKings scoring from stat lines; 100/300-yard bonuses paid as 3 x probability from a lognormal (cv rush 0.55, rec 0.55, pass 0.30); DST points-allowed from a normal around the opponent's implied total (SD 9.5, shutout rate unvalidated)

injury.comment: Gibbs rushed 23 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and secured four of five targets for 20 yards in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Gibbs unsurprisingly had his work cut out for him against the Buccaneers' typically stingy run defense, but the Lions had the luxury of continuing to pound Gibbs into the line while protecting a second-half lead. Gibbs eventually broke through for a game-long 26-yard run and cashed in with one- and four-yard touchdown runs in the fourth quarter to help ice the victory. While Gibbs fell just short of his fifth 100-yard effort in the last six games, the 2023 first-round pick is up to 13 rushing touchdowns and is averaging 5.0 yards per carry heading into a Thanksgiving Day home showdown against the Bears.

injury.comment: Lamb brought 11 of 12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Lamb's near-perfect day included his fifth 100-yard effort of the season -- including his second in the last three games -- and his ninth touchdown grab, which came from eight yards out early in the second quarter. Lamb had six double-digit-yardage catches overall on the afternoon, including his game-long 29-yard grab in the first half. Lamb crossed the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth consecutive season in the process, and he'll take an 88-1,108-9 line into a Week 12 Thanksgiving Day clash at home against the Eagles.

injury.comment: St. Brown brought in five of six targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: St. Brown set the pace for the Lions in catches while also tying for the team lead in targets, and the sure-handed receiver also recorded his eighth touchdown reception of the season on a 14-yard grab early in the second quarter that opened the scoring for either team. St. Brown's yardage total left plenty to be desired, but he's still up to a 70-792-8 line on 97 targets heading into Thursday's holiday showdown at home against the Bears.

injury.comment: Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injury.longComment: Cook extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. He accounted for all but five of Buffalo's rushing attempts as Josh Allen finished without one, but Cook came up short of 100 scrimmage yards for the first time since Week 4. The reigning NFL rushing yards leader continues to put up stellar production heading into Thursday night's home game against the Chiefs.

injury.comment: Allen completed 27 of 45 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injury.longComment: Allen threw a four-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore in the second quarter but got picked off twice later in the first half and had a would-be third interception nullified by a penalty on the penultimate play before halftime. Despite some sloppy play and zero rushing production from Allen, the 9-1 Bills cruised past the 1-9 Dolphins as the star QB raised his season total to 25 touchdowns (14 passing, 11 rushing). Buffalo's likely to encounter more resistance Thursday night against the 8-2 Chiefs. Allen is 5-1 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season but 0-4 when they face off in the playoffs.

injury.comment: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: The 27-year-old RB kept the Panthers' offense afloat nearly single-handedly, as he set a new career high with 172 scrimmage yards while scoring both the team's TDs, on a two-yard run in the first quarter and a one-yard plunge in the fourth. Hubbard's 80 receiving yards were easily a new career high, topping the 3-57-0 line on three targets he recorded in Week 15 of the 2022 season against the Steelers. Over Hubbard's last six games, he surged to 697 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he'll look keep rolling in a Week 11 clash with the Ravens.

injury.comment: Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 24 yards and another score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Williams continued his highly fantasy-friendly season with his third multi-touchdown showing of the season. The veteran back first struck from one yard out to cap off the opening possession of the game, and he added his second scoring grab of 2026 on an 11-yard catch early in the third quarter. Williams has over 60 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's up to 10 rush TDs, his second consecutive double-digit tally, heading into Thursday's home divisional Thanksgiving clash with the Eagles.

injury.comment: Bowers (ankle/quad) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
injury.longComment: Adam Schefter of ESPN previously reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that there was "not a lot of optimism" that Bowers (who was in and out of last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks before exiting for good after halftime due to an ankle injury) would be available versus Denver. Now that he's been made inactive, Bowers -- who was limited at practice Thursday and Friday -- will target a potential Nov. 29 return, while fellow TE Michael Mayer is poised to step into a key role in the Raiders passing offense Sunday in his notable absence.

tg.callText: [lean] Bowers sat out Wednesday's practice but was limited Thursday and Friday, and the final report on Fri Nov 20 lists him as Questionable with no downgrade, even though he said only "We'll see" about playing.

injury.comment: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

injury.comment: Irving rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 32 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Irving worked hard all afternoon against a feisty Lions defense, and outside of his game-long 23-yard run, he scuffled to 45 yards on 17 carries. Irving worked around a hard shot to the abdomen that he sustained in the second half, and he did manage to contribute a rushing touchdown for the fourth straight game when he went in from one yard out in the latter portion of the third quarter. Irving has now equaled a career high with eight rushing touchdowns and is 107 yards short of his second career 1,000-yard season on the ground heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

injury.comment: Swift carried the ball 13 times for 51 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: The Bears' offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye, and Swift wound up leading the backfield in scrimmage yards on the afternoon, highlighting his performance with a three-yard TD pass from Caleb Williams in the second quarter. Swift's 15 touches also led the backfield, as a returning Kyle Monangai got eased back into action with eight touches. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Swift did lose his third fumble of the season, a new career high, but the TD was his 11th of the year, also a new personal best. Monangai could see his workload increase as he puts his turf toe injury further behind him, but Swift seems to have a firm hold of the No. 1 job heading into a Week 12 clash with the team that drafted him in 2020, the Lions.

injury.comment: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
injury.longComment: The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

injury.comment: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
injury.longComment: Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation (or lack thereof) in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.

injury.comment: Pickens secured seven of 10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Pickens played second fiddle to CeeDee Lamb (11-132-1) in Sunday's blowout win, but that still equated to a rewarding effort for the franchise-tagged receiver. The game marked Pickens' third 100-yard effort of the season and second straight, and he now has seen double-digit targets in four of the last six games overall. Pickens rounded out his day Sunday with his sixth touchdown reception of the campaign on a 10-yard catch in the latter portion of the second quarter, and he should be teed up for another busy day when the Cowboys host the Eagles for a Week 12 matchup on Thanksgiving Day.

injury.comment: Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and added four carries for nine yards and another score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As the final score and Prescott's numbers indicate, the prolific passer was clicking on all cylinders right out of the gate against an overmatched Titans defense. Prescott had already helped stake the Cowboys to a 27-6 lead by halftime with eight- and 10-yard touchdown strikes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, respectively. Prescott would strike again through the air in the second half with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Javonte Williams before closing out his scoring strikes with a two-yard toss to Brevyn Spann-Ford with just under five minutes remaining. Prescott added his second rushing touchdown of the campaign on a two-yard run in the latter portion of the third quarter, giving him his second straight five-TD performance. Prescott is up to 3,049 passing yards and a 25:6 TD:INT heading into a Thanksgiving Day home clash with the Eagles in Week 12.

injury.comment: Henry cleared concussion protocol and was made available to the media following Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers, Giana Han of the Baltimore Banner reports.
injury.longComment: Henry was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of the contest, but evidently passed all tests. Prior to his exit, Henry carried 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and hauled in four of his five targets for 17 yards. He also lost his second fumble of the season. Henry looks like he'll be ready to handle his normal role as the lead option out of the Baltimore backfield next Sunday against the Texans.

injury.comment: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.
injury.longComment: The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.

injury.comment: Mahomes completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Mahomes was clicking early against the Cardinals' defense, capping off the opening possession of the game with an eight-yard touchdown toss to Travis Kelce. The prolific signal-caller would go on to add a 22-yard scoring toss to Kelce shortly before the end of the first half, and he capped off his scoring strikes with an 18-yarder to Xavier Worthy in which the speedy receiver sped up the right sideline. Mahomes now has consecutive 300-yard efforts and has accomplished the feat in three of the past four games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 12 showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills on Thanksgiving Night.

injury.comment: Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Pollard eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the third time in the last four games, lighting up his old team for multiple productive gains on the afternoon. The veteran back has been bright spot in a dismal 1-9 start for Tennessee, despite game script often working against the ground attack in the second halves of the Titans' games. Pollard remains firmly on pace for a fifth straight 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

injury.comment: Smith (hamstring) caught five of 12 targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
injury.longComment: Smith was targeted on 12 of Joe Milton's 21 passes in the wide receiver's first game since Week 6. Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass through two starts for the Eagles, so expectations should be tempered for the team's entire passing game, but Smith has reclaimed his role as the team's top pass catcher. Smith could make the most of his hefty target share Thursday against the generous Dallas secondary.

injury.comment: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

injury.comment: Williams completed 15 of 23 passes for 181 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints. He added 11 rushing yards on four carries.
injury.longComment: The Bears' offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye, and both of Williams' TD passes came in the second quarter as he connected with D'Andre Swift on a three-yard shovel pass and Colston Loveland on a 15-yard score. Williams failed to reach 200 passing yards for the first time since Week 2, and he'll take a somewhat disappointing 10:6 TD:INT thorough seven games into a Week 12 clash with the Lions.

injury.comment: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Burden caught two of three targets for 10 yards and added three yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 win over New Orleans.
injury.longComment: It was the worst performance of the season for Burden, who suffered a concussion in the Bears' last game in Week 9 but used a bye week to clear the protocol and avoid missing any additional time. The second-year wideout saw his three-game scoring streak come to an end, and on the season he sports a 51-654-4 line on 69 targets through 10 contests. Burden will look to bounce back in a potential Week 12 barn burner against the Lions.

injury.comment: Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry.
injury.longComment: A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Barkley (left arm) said after Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers that he believes he'll play in Thursday's game at Dallas, Johnny McGonigal of PennLive.com reports.
injury.longComment: Barkley didn't log a touch after the 8:02 mark of the fourth quarter after he had an apparent left arm injury examined by team trainers, according to Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. While Barkley wouldn't elaborate on the issue to McGonigal, the running back seemed optimistic about his chances to suit up in Week 12. Barkley finished Sunday's matchup with 17 carries for 75 yards and one touchdown and wasn't targeted by QB Joe Milton. Monday's injury report may provide further clarity on Barkley's situation.

injury.comment: Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injury.comment: Johnson rushed 23 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 38 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Making a second consecutive start in place of Kenneth Walker (groin), Johnson once again provided starter-quality production as both a runner and receiver. The rookie also added his second career TD on a three-yard run late in the first quarter, making it an all-around rewarding fantasy day. The Chiefs expect Walker to be ready to return for a Thanksgiving Night showdown against the Bills in four days, but even if that comes to pass, Johnson has likely earned himself a larger role for the stretch run with his performance the last two contests.

injury.comment: Moore caught eight of 10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injury.longComment: Moore's four-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter gave him his first multi-game regular-season touchdown streak since Weeks 15 and 16 of the 2025 campaign with the Bears. He briefly left the game later in the first half to have his knee looked at but promptly returned and ultimately reached the 90-yard threshold for a second consecutive game while leading the team in targets. Barring a setback with his knee on a short week, Moore should continue to work as Buffalo's top wide receiver Thanksgiving night against the Chiefs.

injury.comment: Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday that Hall could see a bump in touches for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Howie Kussoy of the New York Post reports.
injury.longComment: "Obviously, [Hall] and Garrett Wilson are guys that we really try to target for the most part...Hall will end up getting a tick more [touches] because, again, he's our starting running back," Glenn said Friday. In his two outings since returning from a five-game absence due to a quad injury, Hall has turned 26 carries into 102 yards (3.9 YPC) while catching seven of eight passes for 93 yards, and he topped 100 scrimmage yards against the Bills in Week 10. Braelon Allen has reverted to RB2 duties in Hall's return, but the former has still been efficient with his touches and is still firmly in the mix for touches despite the return of Hall. The duo will face a Chargers defense Sunday that ranks 15th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (110.2) and limited Derrick Henry to 10 yards on 10 carries (albeit with two touchdowns) in a 23-20 win over the Ravens in Week 10.

injury.comment: Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
injury.longComment: Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Shough is no longer wearing a protect glove on his left (non-throwing) hand at Thursday's practice, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injury.longComment: The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.

injury.comment: Coker entered the league's concussion protocol following Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens, Sheena Quick of Fox Sports Radio 1340 reports.
injury.longComment: Coker was shaken up at the end of a six-yard catch late in the fourth quarter on what appeared to be a helmet-to-helmet hit. He'll have to progress through league's concussion protocol over the next few days, and his status for Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30, is up in the air. He finished Sunday's game with four catches (on seven targets) for 47 yards, and that workload would be absorbed by John Metchie, Brycen Tremayne and Xavier Legette if Coker cannot play against Tampa Bay.

injury.comment: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.
injury.longComment: Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

injury.comment: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.
injury.longComment: Waddle was limited to just 14 snaps and one catch for 22 yards before exiting the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers with a concussion. Following a well-time Week 10 bye, Waddle has progressed through the NFL's concussion protocol, ensuring that Denver's top pass catcher -- who has recorded a 30/337/2 receiving line on 52 targets through nine contests -- will be available this weekend.

injury.comment: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

injury.comment: Tate (shoulder) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
injury.longComment: Tate, who hasn't played since Week 7, had been listed as questionable for the contest despite being a full practice participant Friday. Now that he's back after missing Tennessee's last two games, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft should immediately reclaim a prominent role in the team's offense in a plus matchup, in the absence of any setbacks or limitations. Tate's return to the lineup arrives at an especially opportune time, given fellow WR Wan'Dale Robinson is out for the season after hurting his ankle last weekend. Prior to sustaining his shoulder injury, Tate had made his mark from a fantasy perspective by catching 34 passes on 51 targets for a team-high 413 yards, to go along with a TD through seven games.

injury.comment: Monangai carried the ball eight times for 18 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: Making his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, Monangai wasn't able to generate much offense, as D'Andre Swift led the backfield with 15 touches and 59 scrimmage yards, plus a short receiving TD. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Monangai should see his usage increase as he puts the injury further behind him, and a late lost fumble by Swift -- his third of the season, a new career high -- might encourage coach Ben Johnson to prioritize Monangai even more in Week 12 against the Lions.

injury.comment: Mayfield (foot/thumb) is listed as active Sunday at Detroit, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
injury.longComment: With the Buccaneers on bye in Week 10, Mayfield was front and center following a report from Mike Garafolo of NFL Network last Sunday that the quarterback's status for Week 11 was up in the air due to a foot injury. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network then reported Tuesday that Mayfield "seems to be trending" toward missing Sunday's game. Mayfield then followed up Wednesday's DNP with limited practices Thursday and Friday, entering the weekend listed as questionable. On Saturday, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix reported that Mayfield is tending to a plantar fascia injury, which will require him to wear a special orthotic and new cleats to stabilize the area in order to play. With his availability now confirmed, Mayfield will take on his usual signal-caller duties this weekend, though backup Jalon Daniels is on standby in the event the former needs to come off the field at any point.

tg.callText: [strong] NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Sun Nov 22 that Mayfield will play against the Lions, after he went from missing Wednesday's practice to limited on Thursday and Friday.

injury.comment: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

injury.comment: Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: After accruing his second unsportsmanlike penalty of the contest, Metcalf was tossed from this Week 11 matchup. Prior to his exit with 4:58 remaining in the third quarter, he was having his least productive performance of the season (1-2-0 receiving line on four targets). The Steelers will roll with Germie Bernard, Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and Max Hurleman at wide receiver with Metcalf unavailable for the rest of the game.

injury.comment: Flournoy tallied six catches for 71 yards and one touchdown on seven targets during Sunday's loss to San Francisco. He also recovered a fumble.
injury.longComment: Dallas played catch-up for much of the second half in the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

injury.comment: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week.  ... I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Monday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

injury.comment: Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago.
injury.longComment: Tyson opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a chest injury, but his return to a full practice Friday has him in the clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll look to build upon the 11-80-0 line on 13 targets the he compiled against the Panthers in Week 10.

injury.comment: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
injury.longComment: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

injury.comment: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.
injury.longComment: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

injury.comment: Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injury.comment: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: McConkey (back) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injury.longComment: Though he wasn't among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, back spasms led to McConkey not recording any snaps during the team's 44-22 loss to the Texans on Nov. 8.  After not traveling to Baltimore with his teammates for this past Monday's 23-20 win, the wideout was able to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday through Friday before carrying a 'questionable' designation into the weekend. With no known setbacks since, the 2024 second-rounder will give it a go and is on track to reclaim his key role in Los Angeles' WR corps alongside Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris. In the six games he's taken the field in, McConkey has averaged 2.8 catches (on 4.2 targets) for 47.7 yards with one TD, a pace that the 6-foot, 185-pounder figures to pick up if he can avoid injuries in the coming weeks.

injury.longComment: Meanwhile Carnell Tate (shoulder) is slated to practice this week, and his potential return to action this weekend against Dallas figures to impact the playing time of Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike. Robinson's looming absence will free up snaps/targets in the slot, with Saleh noting Wednesday that he's looking forward to seeing what rookie slot option Xavier Restrepo can do with added opportunities going forward.

injury.comment: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
injury.longComment: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

injury.comment: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too unpredictable to warrant weekly fantasy consideration.

injury.comment: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

injury.comment: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, Mitchell is expected to play an elevated role on offense Sunday against the Chargers.
injury.longComment: Cooper was injured early in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, and Mitchell went on to see eight targets, as the Jets were playing catch-up most of the afternoon. They might be able to keep things closer against the 1-8 Chargers, though Los Angeles is still favored in the contest. Mitchell is a big-play threat as a WR4 for fantasy purposes.

injury.comment: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
injury.longComment: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

injury.comment: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
injury.longComment: The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.

injury.comment: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
injury.longComment: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

injury.comment: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
injury.longComment: Listed as doubtful heading into the weekend after failing to practice in any capacity Wednesday through Friday, Kincaid will wind up missing his first game of the season. Kincaid's 4.5 targets per game will be filtered out among the Bills' other pass-catching options, including Dawson Knox, who will operate as the team's clear No. 1 tight end this week. The Bills will face a quick turnaround for Week 12 with a Thursday matchup versus the Chiefs, so Kincaid may need to practice in some fashion prior to that contest to put himself on a path to play.

injury.comment: Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
injury.longComment: While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. He lost a fumble and took seven sacks in the loss to the Giants, so Milton may need to show that he can avoid negative plays in Week 11 in order to guarantee himself additional starts.

injury.comment: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
injury.longComment: Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.

injury.comment: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injury.longComment: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

injury.comment: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

injury.comment: Kelce brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Kelce tied for the team lead in receptions with Rashee Rice while setting the pace in both receiving yards and targets, and he recorded his first multi-touchdown effort of the season in the process. The legendary tight end recorded his scoring grabs from eight and 22 yards out, and both his reception and yardage totals were his highest since Week 2. Kelce will take a 41-586-4 line into Thursday's Thanksgiving Day road showdown against the Bills.

injury.comment: Beck (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Kansas City, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injury.longComment: The Cardinals were already preparing for Josh Johnson to operate as the starting quarterback Sunday, as Beck entered the weekend with the questionable tag due to back spasms. Joey Aguilar will operate as Johnson's backup, and Beck's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injury.comment: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
injury.longComment: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

Odunze caught all four of his targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: The four grabs led the Bears on the afternoon, as the offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye. Odunze's longest gain went for just 19 yards, and rookie Zavion Thomas wound up leading the team in receiving yards thanks to a 40-yard connection with Caleb Williams in the third quarter. Odunze has caught exactly four passes in four straight games, a stretch in which he's produced a 16-261-1 line on 22 targets. The third-year wideout will try to get more involved in a potential Week 12 barn burner against the Lions.

injury.comment: Lemon will operate as the Eagles' WR2 against the Steelers on Sunday due to the return of DeVonta Smith (hamstring).
injury.longComment: Smith has missed five of the Eagles' last six games (and each of the last three contests) due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver does not carry an injury designation heading into the weekend. Lemon has been the team's WR1 in Smith's absence, but the former still will be heavily involved in the offensive game plan given that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive game. Joe Milton is getting the start at quarterback for a second straight contest, and the Eagles are facing a Steelers defense that ranks 30th in the NFL in receiving yards allowed per game (260.6). Over his last five outings, Lemon has put together a 27-247-1 line on 39 targets.

injury.comment: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
injury.longComment: Brooks was a full practice participant in all three sessions during Week 11 prep. However, the third-year running back is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, and he's slated to miss his eighth consecutive game while recovering from a groin injury. Trevor Etienne, Anthony Tyus and AJ Dillon will continue to operate as the Panthers' backfield depth options behind Chuba Hubbard in the absence of Brooks, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

injury.comment: The Titans placed Spears (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injury.longComment: Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to be the workhorse running back for the Titans while Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton provide depth out of the backfield.

injury.comment: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injury.longComment: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

injury.comment: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
injury.longComment: Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.

injury.comment: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.
injury.longComment: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

injury.comment: Davis (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
injury.longComment: The backup running back was managed during the practice week but is good to go for his normal role behind lead back James Cook. With the Bills listed as 16.5-point favorites, Davis could see some extra reps in garbage time if Buffalo does indeed blow out Miami.

He was carted off the field, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for Johnson to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Salvon Ahmed will move into the RB3 role behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai in Johnson's absence.

injury.comment: Pittman (foot) is not expected to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: Pittman was able to practice fully both Thursday and Friday, but he is not ready to rejoin the mix just yet -- which Pittsburgh confirmed by omitting Pittman from the list of roster moves it made Saturday. Barring an unannounced setback, Pittman figures to continue practicing, and his next chance to take the field will arrive Black Friday, when the Steelers square off against the Broncos.

injury.comment: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.
injury.longComment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Winston carried twice for one yard in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
injury.longComment: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to turn to Winston for quarterback sneaks in future weeks in an effort to limit the wear and tear on McCarthy.

injury.comment: Daniels is set for his usual role as Tampa Bay's backup quarterback Sunday versus Detroit, as Baker Mayfield (foot/thumb) is active and will start, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
injury.longComment: Mayfield entered Sunday deemed questionable due to his injuries, but he's ultimately going to be able to suit up. As such, Daniels will retain his role as Mayfield's backup. Easton Stick (coach's decision) is serving as Tampa Bay's emergency third quarterback.

Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears.
injury.longComment: Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

injury.comment: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

injury.comment: The Eagles placed Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve Saturday.
injury.longComment: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

injury.comment: With Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) inactive for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Mayer is in line to see an expanded role in Week 11.
injury.longComment: Mayer has already carved out his share of looks in the team's passing game, but the absence of Bowers -- who leads the Raiders with 70 targets and 50 catches in eight games played -- creates a big void at tight end on Sunday. In that context, Mayer figures to see added volume versus Denver and represents a viable pivot option for those who roster Bowers, or are otherwise in need of help at the position with six teams on bye.

injury.comment: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
injury.longComment: Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

injury.comment: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that he has no new updates on the status of Conner (foot), who is still "working to return to perform," Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports. "It was not a good injury," LaFleur said.
injury.longComment: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

injury.comment: Mitchell (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
injury.longComment: Mitchell was briefly sidelined with a back injury in the first half before returning to action. The running back is now dealing with an apparent knee issue, placing some doubt on his chances to return to the field Sunday. In his absence, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal will handle the bulk of the workload in the backfield.

injury.comment: Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
injury.longComment: Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

injury.comment: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
injury.longComment: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

injury.comment: Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
injury.longComment: Shipley was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the third-year running back has been officially cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a partial plantar fascia tear that he sustained in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley and Jaydon Blue will operate as the Eagles' rotational running backs behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against a Steelers defense that ranks third in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (83.2).

tg.callText: [lean] The Eagles activated him from injured reserve on Saturday, Nov 21, which teams normally do only when they plan to dress a player, though he is still Questionable after missing Friday's practice with an illness.

injury.comment: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

injury.comment: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

injury.comment: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as Chicago's emergency third quarterback Sunday versus the Saints.
injury.longComment: It's the fifth straight week that Keenum will work as the Bears' emergency third quarterback. That means he can enter Sunday's contest only if both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Broncos' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As the emergency QB3, Ehlinger is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injury.longComment: The rookie seventh-rounder has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026. As the emergency QB3, Nussmeier is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Cook was signed to the Dolphins' active roster Tuesday.
injury.longComment: Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Bears on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As the emergency QB3, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Wilson has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026.

Payton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Steelers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As the emergency third quarterback, Payton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

Johnson will start Sunday's game against the Chiefs with Carson Beck (back) having been downgraded to out for Week 11, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injury.longComment: Coming out of his first NFL start in a Week 10 loss to the Rams, Beck was added to the injury report Thursday due to back spasms. He was listed questionable after failing to practice Friday before the Cardinals offically ruled him out for Week 11 a day later. With Beck set to sit out, the 40-year-old Johnson will pick up his 12th career NFL start while seeing action for his eighth different team since entering the league in 2008 as a fifth-round pick of the Buccaneers. He most recently started in the final two games of the 2025 season as a member of the Commanders, completed 64.4 percent of his passes for 329 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning 11 carries into 55 yards and a score.

injury.comment: Minshew (elbow) underwent UCL reconstructive surgery Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Though the procedure will bring an end to Minshew's season, he's expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 campaign. The veteran quarterback sustained the injury while making his lone start of the season Week 9 in Seattle, but he played though the elbow issue and completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards. Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck took over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in Week 10 and is expected to lead the offense for the remainder of the season.

injury.comment: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
injury.longComment: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

injury.comment: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency quarterback against the Eagles on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As has been the case all year, Howard will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph. As such, Howard is not allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Rodgers and Rudolph leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

Stick (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Lions, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
injury.longComment: The Buccaneers elevated Stick from the team's practice squad Monday. The 31-year-old will only be eligible to play should both Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels exit with an injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Ravens on Sunday, Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.
injury.longComment: King will only play Sunday if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers but will serve as the Ravens' emergency quarterback.
injury.longComment: Slovis will be inactive once again. However, if Jacoby Brissett and Joe Fagnano exit Sunday's meeting with Carolina due to an injury, illness or ejection, Slovis will be available to play.

injury.comment: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

The Bears elevated Ahmed from the practice squad Saturday.
injury.longComment: Even with Kyle Monangai (toe) back from his toe injury for Sunday's game against New Orleans, Ahmed is up as the Bears' fourth running back, though he could be active ahead of Roschon Johnson, who played behind Ahmed in Week 9 against the Bucs.

injury.comment: Abanikanda reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injury.longComment: Abanikanda made his 2026 regular-season debut against the 49ers in Week 10, when he operated as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams. Abanikanda finished that contest with two carries for eight yards and a two-yard catch on his lone target in what ended as a 46-40 loss for Dallas. With both Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) on injured reserve, Abanikanda figures to be elevated to the Cowboys' active roster for Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday.

Corbin was elevated from the Cowboys' practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Corbin signed with the Cowboys' practice squad Nov. 4, and Saturday was his first elevation to the 53-man roster. With Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) both on injured reserve, Corbin will operate as Dallas' RB2 behind workhorse Javonte Williams. Corbin last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he appeared in six games as a member of the Giants.

The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Susanna Weir of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Schrader's elevation is his third of the season, so he'll need to be signed to Denver's active roster in order to see game action for the team beyond Sunday. In his previous two appearances, the third-year pro played a total of two offensive snaps and nine snaps on special teams without recording any carries or targets. Schrader isn't likely to be much of a factor on offense Sunday against Las Vegas, as Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins should continue to lead the Broncos' backfield. However, Schrader could contribute as a kick returner -- he's tallied 68 yards on three kickoff returns this season.

injury.comment: Prentice (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injury.longComment: It appears Prentice entered the league's concussion protocol following the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers. He had additional time to recover courtesy of the Week 10 bye, so the veteran fullback should be available for Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Raiders.

injury.comment: Saylors rushed twice for nine yards while adding 26 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.
injury.longComment: Saylors played six snaps on offense while serving as a No. 3 option behind Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki in the backfield. Saylors was on the field for 20 snaps with the special-teams unit, and he'll continue to be primarily a special-teams asset in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

Chestnut played all 25 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: The fifth-year running back has suited up for all nine of the Titans' games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams as a member of the team's kick coverage and return units. He's played just two offensive snaps on the campaign and hasn't logged any carries or targets.

injury.comment: Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injury.longComment: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

injury.comment: The Chiefs elevated Carter from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
injury.longComment: Carter has been brought up from the practice squad for a second consecutive week to give the Chiefs more depth in the backfield in the absence of Kenneth Walker (groin). Carter operated as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson in Week 10 against the Falcons, but the former's role could be limited to special-teams duties since Jaydn Ott (hamstring) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence.

injury.comment: VanSumeren (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: VanSumeran injured his knee in the second half, and with no other fullback on the 53-man roster, the Chiefs could turn to tight end Jake Briningstool to provide additional blocking out of the backfield. VanSumeran's status over the coming days will be worth monitoring, given that the Chiefs are operating on a short week and play against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

injury.comment: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
injury.longComment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injury.longComment: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

injury.comment: The Giants elevated Mafah from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: It's the second time this season that Mafah has been promoted to the 53-man roster, with the first instance being Week 10 against the Eagles. His elevation gives the Giants another contributor on special teams and extra depth in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers.

injury.comment: Davis didn't touch the ball on offense in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.
